newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depos, bonds idle but drachma up vs ecu late.
newsitem.headline: Greek depos, bonds idle but drachma up vs ecu late.

text.p: The drachma stayed in a range against the ecu, firming 10 ticks to 308.50 in late Monday dealings after the central bank sold 60 million ecus for drachmas at the fixing, dealers said.
Depos, forex forwards and bonds were little changed, holding midsession levels, dealers said.
"The central bank's move to sell 60 million ecus for drachmas at the fixing showed its determination to honour its commitment to the hard drachma policy," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank.
Ecu/drachma spent most of the session in the 308.45/60 corridor after opening at 308.40/50.
"Ecu/drachma is hovering around 308.50 in late trade, off an intraday high of 308.85," he said.

Fixed coupon bonds and FRNs were fluctuating narrowly, holding midday prices in late trading, unaffected by the finance ministry's announcement pertaining to the amount of the FRN auction on August 21 and fresh cuts in T-bill rates, dealers said.
The finance ministry will seek to raise 100 billion drachmas via its FRN auction.

"The amount was expected, and the market did not react to the news," said a foreign bank dealer. "The key is liquidity, and it looks if the system will get some help from regular, end-month inflows from pension funds."

The treasury will also cut three-, six- and 12-month T-bill rates by 10 basis points to 8.4 percent, 8.7 percent and 9.5 percent, respectively, from Tuesday. It will also offer 12-month T-bills to the public on August 20.
The 10-year bond was trading around 94.50 in late dealings, sustaining its 402 basis point spread over Bunds, dealers said.
The market was quoted at 156.97/07 from Monday's 157.195 fix, the dollar at 285.97/07 from 285.470 and the ecu at 308.34/44 from 308.600.
